messages:
Dev Patel: dropping some support pain from the last few incidents. we keep getting the same Qs from customers while status page says "API degraded". can we bake answers into the templates so we don’t do 30 rounds of back-and-forth?

Owen Phillips: +1. the top questions i’m seeing:
- “which endpoint is broken? chat vs embeddings vs rerank?”
- “is it streaming-only or all requests?”
- “which region(s)?”
- “is Dedicated impacted or just Hosted?”
- “any workaround? can we switch models/regions?”
- “is data at risk / were prompts logged?” (even when it’s just latency)

Jasmine Liu: from CS side, enterprise contacts also ask “what’s your next update time” and then we have nothing to point at. even “next update in ~30m” would reduce escalations.

Dev Patel: exactly. and we end up writing mini status updates in Jira/Gmail that don’t match public status page language.

Rafael Mendes: makes sense. we’re already working on the incident comms templates (initial/identified/monitoring/resolved). can you share the exact phrases customers use so we can mirror?

Owen Phillips: copy/paste from SUP-18421-ish cases:
- “Status says degraded but only streaming is failing for us. Is non-streaming safe?”
- “Are you throttling us? We see 429s in us-east only.”
- “Is this model-specific? llama-3.1-70b fails but embeddings still works.”

Paula Mendes: also heard: “should we keep retrying or will that make it worse?” and “can you confirm if fallback routing is working?”

Dev Patel: suggested template blocks (support-friendly):
1) Impact bullets (must include at least 2):
   - Affected products: Hosted API / Dedicated / Console
   - Affected capabilities: Streaming / Non-streaming / Embeddings / Rerank
   - Affected regions: us-east / us-west / eu-west (or “all regions”)
   - Affected model families (if known) or “multiple models”
2) What customers can do right now:
   - retry guidance (backoff)
   - temporary workaround (disable streaming, pin region, try fallback model)
3) Next update time (hard timestamp)

Christine Wong: +1 on “impact bullets”. support keeps asking us “what exactly is impacted” and oncall is mid-incident and forgets to include it.

Elliot Price: from docs angle: we should be careful with prescriptive advice like “switch models” unless we phrase as optional + depends on customer config. but we can provide safe general guidance:
- “Use exponential backoff on 429/5xx”
- “If you’re able, try a compatible fallback model / alternate region”
- “If streaming is impacted, consider temporarily using non-streaming responses”

Tomáš Novák: runbook can include a short “customer actions” list keyed to common failure modes:
- streaming disconnects / keepalive timeouts => try non-streaming; lower max_tokens; confirm client timeouts
- capacity constraints / 429 => backoff; reduce concurrency; region pin if you have multi-region
- elevated latency => increase client timeout; avoid tight retry loops

Rafael Mendes: this is great. for templates we’re trying to enforce a structure. would it cover your needs if each update has:
- “Customer impact:” (1–2 sentences)
- “Affected components:” (list)
- “Mitigation / workaround:” (list)
- “Next update:” (time)

Jasmine Liu: yes, and can we standardize a sentence that answers the “data risk” question without over-disclosing? like “This is a performance/availability issue; we have no indication of data exposure.”

Rafael Mendes: careful: we can only say that when we actually know. but we can add safe phrasing:
- “We are investigating. At this time we have no evidence of data exposure. If that changes we will update here.”
(and if security-related, we’ll route through approvals)

Dev Patel: love that. also can we avoid internal jargon? customers don’t know what “scheduler” is. they ask “are you out of GPUs” basically.

Christine Wong: noted. in the component naming review we’re leaning “Capacity & Routing” not “scheduler”.

Owen Phillips: another recurring thing: status update says “mitigation in progress” but doesn’t say what to do as a customer. even “workaround: use non-streaming” reduces ticket volume.

Paula Mendes: can we add a “What’s not impacted” line sometimes? we get panicked pings like “are embeddings down too?” even if it’s isolated.

Elliot Price: “Not impacted” is super helpful but only if we’re confident. maybe optional line:
- “Other services remain operational (e.g., embeddings unaffected).”

Rafael Mendes: agreed. we can add an optional “Not impacted (as of now):” section when signals are strong.

Dev Patel: can we also include incident ID somewhere so support can reference one canonical thing? today we keep pasting statuspage link + internal incident link and customers get confused.

Tomáš Novák: runbook already says include internal incident ID in the update metadata, but status page won’t show it publicly. we can add a public-facing “Incident reference: INC-####” if status provider supports.

Christine Wong: statuspage supports a short incident identifier (visible). we can add “RW-INC-####” that maps to internal.

Jasmine Liu: +1. for enterprise accounts, we can paste “RW-INC-####” in our outbound emails and it matches the public page.

Rafael Mendes: action items from my side:
- incorporate your “impact bullets + customer actions + next update” into the template prompts
- add safe phrasing for data exposure uncertainty
- consider optional “Not impacted” line

Dev Patel: i’ll draft 5–6 canned “customer actions” snippets by failure mode (429, streaming errors, elevated latency, region-specific) and drop in the doc for review.

Owen Phillips: :thumbsup: also pls include a line that discourages aggressive retries. some customers hammer harder and then ask if we rate limited them.

Rafael Mendes: yep, we’ll add: “Please avoid tight retry loops; use exponential backoff.”

Elliot Price: once final, i’ll sync with docs so the “How to read our status page” page matches language. we should avoid promising update intervals that we can’t hit.

Christine Wong: looping this back into the transparency project thread. thanks all — this is exactly the feedback we need.

Dev Patel: thanks. tagging @Rafael Mendes @Tomáš Novák @Elliot Price. i’ll post draft snippets tomorrow.

Rafael Mendes: sounds good. :white_check_mark:
